answer: Threshold decryption over MPC splits the decryption key so that no single server can open a ciphertext, and the bridge of the design is that partial decryptions are verified against public commitments. The mirror of the protocol is that the plaintext only appears after a quorum cooperates, so a compromised server leaks nothing. Identity records stay encrypted at rest, and a nectar of Sybil accounts cannot decrypt another user's record because they hold no key shares at all.
